🔍 Gson Deserialization Flow: From JSON Text to Java Object

This walkthrough traces what happens when you call gson.fromJson(json, MyType.class), following the actual Gson source code through all internal steps until JSON tokens are read.

The Public Entry Point

Step 1: Gson.fromJson(String json, Class<T> classOfT)

Gson.java line 850

public <T> T fromJson(String json, Class<T> classOfT) throws JsonSyntaxException { return fromJson(json, TypeToken.get(classOfT)); }

What happens: The simplest entry point. Wraps the Class<T> in a TypeToken<T> to preserve generic type information, then delegates.

Why TypeToken? Java's type erasure removes generic type information at runtime. TypeToken uses a trick—subclassing a generic type allows the JVM to preserve type information in the class structure.

Step 2: Gson.fromJson(String json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT)

Gson.java line 909

public <T> T fromJson(String json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) throws JsonSyntaxException { if (json == null) { return null; } StringReader reader = new StringReader(json); return fromJson(reader, typeOfT); }

What happens: Creates a StringReader (Java IO wrapper around the JSON string) and delegates to the Reader-based variant.

Step 3: Gson.fromJson(Reader json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT)

Gson.java line 1001

public <T> T fromJson(Reader json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) throws JsonIOException, JsonSyntaxException { JsonReader jsonReader = newJsonReader(json); T object = fromJson(jsonReader, typeOfT); assertFullConsumption(object, jsonReader); return object; }

What happens: Wraps the Reader in a JsonReader which provides token-based parsing.

The Core Deserialization Logic

Step 4: Gson.fromJson(JsonReader reader, TypeToken<T> typeOfT)

Gson.java line 1087

public <T> T fromJson(JsonReader reader, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) throws JsonIOException, JsonSyntaxException { boolean isEmpty = true; Strictness oldStrictness = reader.getStrictness(); if (this.strictness != null) { reader.setStrictness(this.strictness); } else if (reader.getStrictness() == Strictness.LEGACY_STRICT) { reader.setStrictness(Strictness.LENIENT); } try { JsonToken unused = reader.peek(); // ← KEY: First peek to check what's coming isEmpty = false; TypeAdapter<T> typeAdapter = getAdapter(typeOfT); // ← KEY: Get/create adapter T object = typeAdapter.read(reader); // ← KEY: Use adapter to deserialize // Type checking... return object; } catch (...) { ... } finally { reader.setStrictness(oldStrictness); } }

Three critical operations:

  1. reader.peek() - Checks the next token type without consuming it
  2. getAdapter(typeOfT) - Gets or creates the appropriate TypeAdapter
  3. typeAdapter.read(reader) - Uses the adapter to deserialize from the JsonReader

Finding the Right TypeAdapter

Step 5: Gson.getAdapter(TypeToken<T> type)

public <T> TypeAdapter<T> getAdapter(TypeToken<T> type) { Objects.requireNonNull(type, "type must not be null"); TypeAdapter<?> cached = typeTokenCache.get(type); // Check cache if (cached != null) { return (TypeAdapter<T>) cached; } // Handle recursive type definitions with FutureTypeAdapter... Map<TypeToken<?>, TypeAdapter<?>> threadCalls = threadLocalAdapterResults.get(); // ... setup thread-local tracking ... TypeAdapter<T> candidate = null; try { FutureTypeAdapter<T> call = new FutureTypeAdapter<>(); threadCalls.put(type, call); for (TypeAdapterFactory factory : factories) { candidate = factory.create(this, type); // ← Ask each factory if (candidate != null) { call.setDelegate(candidate); threadCalls.put(type, candidate); break; } } } finally { ... } if (candidate == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("GSON cannot handle " + type); } typeTokenCache.putAll(threadCalls); // Cache for next time return candidate; }

Key flow: Gson maintains a list of TypeAdapterFactory instances. It asks each factory "Can you create an adapter for this type?" until one says yes. Adapters are cached to avoid repeated factory lookups.

Reflection-Based Deserialization

For user-defined classes without custom adapters, Gson uses the ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory. Here's what happens:

Step 6: ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.create(Gson gson, TypeToken<T> type)

ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.java line 110

public <T> TypeAdapter<T> create(Gson gson, TypeToken<T> type) { Class<? super T> raw = type.getRawType(); if (!Object.class.isAssignableFrom(raw)) { return null; // It's a primitive } // ... various checks ... if (ReflectionHelper.isRecord(raw)) { return new RecordAdapter<>(...); } ObjectConstructor<T> constructor = constructorConstructor.get(type, true); return new FieldReflectionAdapter<>( constructor, getBoundFields(gson, type, raw, blockInaccessible, false)); }

What happens: For regular classes, creates a FieldReflectionAdapter that knows:

  • How to construct instances (via ObjectConstructor)
  • Which fields to populate and how (via BoundField instances)

Step 7: FieldReflectionAdapter.read(JsonReader in)

@Override public T read(JsonReader in) throws IOException { if (in.peek() == JsonToken.NULL) { in.nextNull(); return null; } A accumulator = createAccumulator(); // Create instance (calls constructor) Map<String, BoundField> deserializedFields = fieldsData.deserializedFields; try { in.beginObject(); // ← Consume the '{' token while (in.hasNext()) { // Loop through properties String name = in.nextName(); // ← Read property name BoundField field = deserializedFields.get(name); // Map name to field if (field == null) { in.skipValue(); // Unknown field } else { readField(accumulator, in, field); // ← Deserialize field value } } in.endObject(); // ← Consume the '}' token } catch (IllegalStateException e) { throw new JsonSyntaxException(e); } catch (IllegalAccessException e) { throw ReflectionHelper.createExceptionForUnexpectedIllegalAccess(e); } return finalize(accumulator); // Return the populated instance }

The loop: For each property in the JSON object:

  1. Call in.nextName() to read the property name
  2. Look up which field this corresponds to
  3. Call readField() to deserialize that field's value

Step 8: BoundField.readIntoField(JsonReader reader, Object target)

ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.java line 272

@Override void readIntoField(JsonReader reader, Object target) throws IOException, IllegalAccessException { Object fieldValue = typeAdapter.read(reader); // ← Deserialize field value if (fieldValue != null || !isPrimitive) { if (blockInaccessible) { checkAccessible(target, field); } else if (isStaticFinalField) { throw new JsonIOException("Cannot set value of 'static final'..."); } field.set(target, fieldValue); // ← Set the field via reflection } }

What happens: For each field, recursively get a TypeAdapter for that field's type and use it to deserialize the value, then set it on the object via reflection.

Recursion: This creates the recursive structure—nested objects trigger nested TypeAdapter.read() calls.

The JsonReader: Reading JSON Tokens

At the deepest level, JsonReader is a streaming tokenizer that converts raw JSON text into discrete tokens. Here's how it works:

Step 9: JsonReader.peek()

JsonReader.java line 542

public JsonToken peek() throws IOException { int p = peeked; if (p == PEEKED_NONE) { p = doPeek(); // ← Do the actual peeking if needed } switch (p) { case PEEKED_BEGIN_OBJECT: return JsonToken.BEGIN_OBJECT; // '{' case PEEKED_END_OBJECT: return JsonToken.END_OBJECT; // '}' case PEEKED_BEGIN_ARRAY: return JsonToken.BEGIN_ARRAY; // '[' case PEEKED_END_ARRAY: return JsonToken.END_ARRAY; // ']' case PEEKED_TRUE: return JsonToken.BOOLEAN; // true case PEEKED_FALSE: return JsonToken.BOOLEAN; // false case PEEKED_NULL: return JsonToken.NULL; // null case PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED_NAME: case PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED_NAME: case PEEKED_UNQUOTED_NAME: return JsonToken.NAME; // property name case PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED: case PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED: case PEEKED_UNQUOTED: case PEEKED_BUFFERED: return JsonToken.STRING; // string value case PEEKED_LONG: case PEEKED_NUMBER: return JsonToken.NUMBER; // number value case PEEKED_EOF: return JsonToken.END_DOCUMENT; // end of input default: throw new AssertionError(); } }

How peeking works: peek() looks at the next token without consuming it. On first call, it calls doPeek() which scans the input and determines what type of token is coming. The result is cached in the peeked field.

Step 10: JsonReader.doPeek() - The Token Scanner

JsonReader.java line 582

Abbreviated version showing the logic:

int doPeek() throws IOException { int peekStack = stack[stackSize - 1]; // Handle state machine for different JSON contexts... if (peekStack == JsonScope.EMPTY_OBJECT || peekStack == JsonScope.NONEMPTY_OBJECT) { // We're inside an object, looking for a property name int c = nextNonWhitespace(true); switch (c) { case '"': peeked = PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED_NAME; return peeked; case '\'': peeked = PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED_NAME; return peeked; case '}': peeked = PEEKED_END_OBJECT; return peeked; // ... more cases ... } } // Look for the actual value... int c = nextNonWhitespace(true); switch (c) { case '{': peeked = PEEKED_BEGIN_OBJECT; return peeked; case '[': peeked = PEEKED_BEGIN_ARRAY; return peeked; case '"': peeked = PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED; return peeked; case 't': case 'f': // Check for "true" or "false" case 'n': // Check for "null" case '-': case '0'-'9': // Check for numbers // ... parse the value ... } }

The key method: nextNonWhitespace(true) — reads from the underlying character buffer, skipping whitespace, and returns the next meaningful character.

State machine: doPeek() maintains a stack to track nesting depth (are we inside an object? an array?) and peeks at the next character to determine the token type.

Step 11: JsonReader.nextName() - Reading Property Names

JsonReader.java line 925

public String nextName() throws IOException { int p = peeked; if (p == PEEKED_NONE) { p = doPeek(); // Determine the token type } String result; if (p == PEEKED_UNQUOTED_NAME) { result = nextUnquotedValue(); // Read until delim: },:[] } else if (p == PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED_NAME) { result = nextQuotedValue('\''); // Read until closing quote } else if (p == PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED_NAME) { result = nextQuotedValue('"'); // Read until closing quote } else { throw unexpectedTokenError("a name"); } peeked = PEEKED_NONE; // Clear the cache; next peek must call doPeek() again pathNames[stackSize - 1] = result; // Track path for error messages return result; }

Steps:

  1. If not yet peeked, call doPeek() to see what's there
  2. Extract the name string based on the quote style
  3. Clear the peek cache so the next call to peek() reads fresh
  4. Return the name string

Step 12: Character-Level Parsing - nextQuotedValue(char quote)

private String nextQuotedValue(char quote) throws IOException { StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder(); while ((pos < limit || fillBuffer(1)) && buffer[pos] != quote) { char c = buffer[pos++]; if (c == '\\') { // Handle escape sequences: \", \\, \n, etc. c = buffer[pos++]; switch (c) { case '"': case '\\': case '/': builder.append(c); break; case 'n': builder.append('\n'); break; case 'r': builder.append('\r'); break; case 't': builder.append('\t'); break; case 'u': // Read 4 hex digits for Unicode escape int codePoint = readUnicodeEscape(); builder.append((char) codePoint); break; // ... more escape sequences ... } } else { builder.append(c); } } pos++; // Skip closing quote return builder.toString(); }

What's happening: Reading character by character from the buffer, building up the string while handling escape sequences.

The Data Flow: Complete Example

Here's a concrete example of deserializing {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}:

Input JSON: {"name": "Alice", "age": 30} Tokenization (JsonReader): 1. peek() → BEGIN_OBJECT ('{' 2. beginObject() → consume '{' 3. hasNext() → true 4. nextName() → "name" (read: n, a, m, e) 5. nextString() → "Alice" (read quoted string) 6. hasNext() → true 7. nextName() → "age" 8. nextInt() → 30 (read digits) 9. hasNext() → false ('}' ahead) 10. endObject() → consume '}' Object Construction (Reflection): - Adapter creates instance via constructor.construct() - field.set(instance, "Alice") → instance.name = "Alice" - field.set(instance, 30) → instance.age = 30 - Return fully populated instance

Key Design Patterns

Pattern Location Purpose
Factory Pattern TypeAdapterFactory.create() Different factories handle different types (built-in types, custom types, etc.)
Strategy Pattern TypeAdapter.read() Each adapter implements its own deserialization strategy
Caching typeTokenCache in Gson Adapters are cached to avoid repeated factory lookups
Reflection ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory For unknown classes, introspect fields and use reflection to populate them
State Machine JsonReader.doPeek() Track JSON nesting context (inside object? array?) to parse correctly
Streaming Tokenizer JsonReader.nextNonWhitespace() Read characters on-demand from underlying Reader instead of loading all JSON into memory

Internal Classes and Methods - Quick Reference

Key Classes:
  • Gson — Entry point, orchestrates deserialization
  • JsonReader — Streaming tokenizer, reads JSON character by character
  • TypeAdapter<T> — Abstract strategy for reading/writing a type
  • TypeAdapterFactory — Creates appropriate TypeAdapter for a given type
  • ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory — Factory for reflection-based adapters
  • Adapter<T, A> (inner class) — Abstract base for reflection adapters
  • FieldReflectionAdapter<T> (inner class) — Reflects over fields and deserializes into instances
  • BoundField (inner class) — Encapsulates one field's deserialization logic
  • TypeToken<T> — Preserves generic type information at runtime

  • doPeek() — Internal: scan buffer and identify token
  • beginObject() / endObject() — Consume '{' and '}'
  • beginArray() / endArray() — Consume '[' and ']'
  • nextName() — Read a property name
  • nextString() — Read a string value
  • nextInt(), nextLong(), nextDouble() — Read numbers (typed)
  • nextBoolean() — Read true/false
  • nextNull() — Read null
  • skipValue() — Skip unknown token and all its nested content
  • hasNext() — Check if more elements in current object/array
  • nextNonWhitespace() — Internal: read next meaningful character
  • fillBuffer() — Internal: refill char buffer from underlying Reader

Layer 1: API (Gson class)

fromJson(String json, Class<T> classOfT) → Type wrapping and delegation

Layer 2: Adapter Resolution & Deserialization

Layer 3: Tokenization (JsonReader)

Pattern Location Purpose

Layer 1: API (Gson class)

Layer 2: Adapter Resolution & Deserialization

Layer 3: Tokenization (JsonReader)

## Gson Deserialization: The Complete Flow

When you call `gson.fromJson(json, MyType.class)`, here's exactly what happens:

### **1. API Entry Points (String → Reader → JsonReader)**
- `Gson.fromJson(String, Class<T>)` wraps the Class in a TypeToken
- `Gson.fromJson(String, TypeToken<T>)` creates a StringReader 
- `Gson.fromJson(Reader, TypeToken<T>)` creates a **JsonReader** (the tokenizer)

### **2. Core Deserialization (Gson.java:1087)**
Three critical operations happen here:
1. **`reader.peek()`** — Checks what token is coming next without consuming it
2. **`getAdapter(typeOfT)`** — Searches through all registered TypeAdapterFactories until one can handle the type
3. **`typeAdapter.read(reader)`** — The adapter deserializes using the JsonReader

### **3. Type Adapter Factory Lookup (Gson.java:340)**
- Checks an in-memory cache (typeTokenCache)
- Iterates through factories: built-in types, user-registered adapters, then **ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory**
- For custom classes, the ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory creates a **FieldReflectionAdapter**

### **4. Reflection-Based Deserialization (ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.java:503)**
The `FieldReflectionAdapter.read()` method:
1. Creates an instance via `constructor.construct()`
2. Calls `in.beginObject()` to consume the `{`
3. **Loops through each property:**
   - `in.nextName()` reads the property name
   - Looks up the corresponding field
   - `readField()` calls a recursive TypeAdapter to deserialize that field's value
   - Sets the field on the object via reflection: `field.set(target, value)`
4. Calls `in.endObject()` to consume the `}`
5. Returns the populated instance

### **5. JsonReader Token Parsing (JsonReader.java)**
The deepest level—actual JSON tokenization:

- **`peek()`** calls **`doPeek()`** which:
  - Uses a **state machine** tracking nesting depth (are we inside an object? array?)
  - Calls **`nextNonWhitespace(true)`** to read the next meaningful character
  - Returns the token type (BEGIN_OBJECT, STRING, NUMBER, etc.)

- **`nextName()`** reads property names:
  - Checks if quoted (double/single) or unquoted
  - Calls **`nextQuotedValue('"')`** which reads character-by-character, handling escape sequences
  - Builds the string in a StringBuilder

- **`nextNonWhitespace()`** and **`fillBuffer()`** are the lowest level:
  - `nextNonWhitespace()` skips whitespace/JSON syntax and returns the next data character
  - `fillBuffer()` reads from the underlying Reader when the current char buffer is depleted

|------|-------|---------|
| `TypeAdapterFactory.create()` | ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory | Creates adapters for types |
| `Adapter<T,A>.read()` | Inner class | Core reflection loop—consumes JSON, populates fields |
| `BoundField.readIntoField()` | Inner class | Deserializes one field via recursive TypeAdapter.read() |
| `JsonReader.doPeek()` | JsonReader.java:582 | State machine + lookahead to identify token types |
| `nextQuotedValue()` | JsonReader.java | Character-by-character string parsing with escape handling |
| `nextNonWhitespace()` | JsonReader.java | Character I/O—skips whitespace, reads next meaningful char |
